#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      # The ref THIS awf repo was invoked at — a reusable workflow runs in
      # the CALLER's context, so github.workflow_ref carries the caller's ref
      # (dart's branch), which is meaningless against the awf remote. The
      # stub passes its own pin here (main in production) — same pattern as
      factory_home_ref:
        description: Awf ref the caller pinned factory-teammate.yml to
        type: string
        required: false
        default: main
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      # Optional agent-work toolchains (salvaged from #35): "" (default)
      # installs NOTHING — explicit opt-in per caller. The dmtools engine
      # and its dart runtime are installed by install-dmtools-cli.sh and
      # are NEVER gated on these inputs.
      java-version:
        description: 'JDK for agent work (Temurin, Gradle/Maven cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "21".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      node-version:
        description: 'Node.js for agent work (npm cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "20".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      python-version:
        description: 'Python for agent work. "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "3.12".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" (default) installs NOTHING — most consumers are not Flutter projects and bring their own toolchain via the setup/install scripts. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0"); Flutter targets (fa) pass it explicitly.'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 1 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 2 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 3 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 1 — value lands in the agent job env under CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME. The factory never knows key names; the caller stub documents which repo secret maps here.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 2 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 3 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  guard:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.

      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \

            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"

      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

**CONFIRMED — this is the root cause of bug 1.**

- The actions/checkout-style shallow single-branch clone has `remote.origin.fetch = +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`.
- `git fetch --depth 1 origin refs/heads/fa-sess/gh-925` SUCCEEDS (writes FETCH_HEAD) but does **NOT** create `refs/remotes/origin/fa-sess/gh-925`.
- Then `git checkout refs/remotes/origin/fa-sess/gh-925 -- .dmtools/fa-sessions` → the ref doesn't resolve → git treats BOTH as pathspecs → the observed `error: pathspec '.dmtools/fa-sessions' did not match any file(s) known to git` → exit 1 under `bash -e`.

So the restore works ONLY when the branch doesn't exist (fetch fails → else) and DIES whenever the branch exists — i.e., every retry/second leg of a fresh issue dies. That's exactly the 2/2 repro. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"

    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.

      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \

            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"

      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"

      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi

  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

`git fetch origin refs/heads/X` writes FETCH_HEAD; whether it creates refs/remotes/origin/X depends on git version/config (opportunistic update happens only when the fetched ref matches an existing fetch refspec's RHS pattern — in single-branch clones with refspec `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, fetching fa-sess/X does NOT match → no tracking ref). This also matches the ticket note: "dart/fa dev legs masked this because their issues had prior sessions" — hmm, wait. Actually re-read: "Note: dart/fa dev legs masked this because their issues had prior sessions." #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
  fi
  if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
    echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
  fi
  # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
  # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
  # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 —…

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:

        run: |

               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then

          fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Decide whether this event is for the agent) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
  if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
    exit 1
  fi

  # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
  # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
  # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
  # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
  if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
    echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
    exit 1
  fi
  RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
  RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
  RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
  RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
  echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

  # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
  # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
  # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
  # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
  # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
  # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
  # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
  # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
  # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
  rework_override_ok() {
    if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$perm" in
      admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
      *)
        echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  }

  # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
  # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
  # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
  # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
  # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$state" ]; then
      # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
      # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
      echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
      exit 0
    fi
    # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
    # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
    pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
      --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
      exit 0
    fi
    leg="$INPUT_LEG"
    if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
      leg="rework"
    fi
    if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
      if ! rework_override_ok; then
        echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # RACE GUARD (live: agents #934, 2026-10-16 — an `assigned` and a
  # `labeled` event for one issue BOTH passed the fresh-label refresh
  # before either applied its status labels; the per-issue concurrency
  # group (cancel-in-progress: false) queued both — duplicate legs).
  # An EVENT-triggered run self-cancels when a sibling leg already
  # carries the anchor: in_progress, or queued with an EARLIER run id
  # (the elder twin wins). Explicit dispatches (inputs.leg) always win
  # and never self-cancel. Title match is "#N" — the issues-event echo
  # shape ("teammate: issues #N"); PR-anchored dispatches spell
  # pr-N/gh-N and do not collide.
  if [ -z "${INPUT_LEG:-}" ]; then
    sibling="$(gh run list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
      --workflow "${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" --limit 30 \
      --json databaseId,status,displayTitle \
      --jq ".[] | select(.databaseId != ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}) \
            | select(.status == \"in_progress\" or (.status == \"queued\" and .databaseId < ${GITHUB_RUN_ID})) \
            | select(.displayTitle | contains(\"#${NUMBER}\")) | .databaseId" \
      | head -1)"
    if [ -n "$sibling" ]; then
      echo "::notice::race guard: sibling run ${sibling} already carries #${NUMBER} — self-cancelling (event echo)"
      gh run cancel "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
      sleep 10
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
  # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
  # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
  # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
  # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
  # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
  # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
  # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
  # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
  # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
  if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
    && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
    LABELS="$fresh_labels"
    ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
  else
    echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then

            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
